root_cause: The live AI Modelwijzer catalog covered 103 models across 10 provider families but omitted TII/Falcon entirely, despite Falcon being decision-relevant for open-weight, local, edge and customer-controlled deployments. Provider completeness had been measured mostly by total model count rather than explicit family coverage.
prevention: Maintain provider-family coverage as an explicit invariant in addition to total model count.
Keep TII/Falcon represented in the canonical catalog with official-source evidence and at least one general/reasoning model plus one specialist model.
For open-weight models, separate model identity from deployment-path governance: self-hosting can make storage and inference customer-controlled, but does not itself guarantee EU location.
Unknown managed-hosting price, retention, subprocessors or residency must remain provider-dependent rather than being inferred.
fix: Add TII/Falcon as provider family 11 with Falcon H1, Falcon H1R and Falcon OCR decision records; add a self-host/customer-cloud/on-prem governance path; add official TII source authority; bind Falcon coverage into the AI Model Intelligence skill and canonical System Map.
